newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Cogentrix case to be heard this month.
newsitem.headline: India says Cogentrix case to be heard this month.

text.p: A case involving U.S. power firm Cogentrix Inc will be heard by a state high court later this month, Indian power secretary P. Abraham said on Friday.
"A date for the Cogentrix hearing has been fixed in the last week of January," Abraham, the highest ranking civil servant in the Power Ministry, told Reuters. He did not give the date.

Last month the Supreme Court declined to rule on a demand that five infrastructure projects including a high-profile project by Cogentrix be halted on environmental grounds. The Supreme Court asked the southern state of Karnataka to rule on Cogentrix's project.
"All issues were finalised and all clearances had come through but then they got into this environmental case," Abraham said.
Cogentrix is building a 1,000 megawatt plant in a joint venture with a unit of China Light and Power Co Ltd.
Abraham said frequent public interest litigation was one factor which dissuaded global private firms from investing in core sectors including power.
"People do not come to India to go to court and meet lawyers. They come here to put their project and make money. Enron has gone through 22 cases," Abraham said.
He was referring to U.S.-based Enron Development Corp, which is building a 2,450 megawatt plant in the western state of Maharashtra.
"They (investors) don't want to waste their time. India is not the only country," Abraham said.
